_comment: dreamteam tunables. All hooks/scripts read this via jq with the same defaults baked in, so it works even if this file is absent. Calibrated to the VERIFIED 2026-06-30 OOM postmortem on katana (32 GB RAM / 32 GB swap): 59 distinct Claude procs at OOM time, TWO simultaneous balloons (3.7 GB + 3.4 GB), 17.2 GB resident; baseline ~200-280 MB/agent.

_notes.maxAgents: SYSTEM-WIDE cap (mem-gate counts ALL claude procs via pgrep, not just this team). 59 ran on 06-30 across multiple sessions — a per-team cap can't see the aggregate; this can. Raised 30→36 on 2026-07-01 after the cap (not memory) became the binding constraint during a real multi-fleet day (31 procs, budget said 7 more agents fit); the memory budget + 8G floor remain the true guards, and 36 still sits well under the 59-proc disaster load.
_notes.perAgentMB: Planning RSS for a NEW agent. Verified baseline at OOM time was ~200-280 MB; live-active with context ~350-430 MB. Set to 300 (2026-07-01) — the measured baseline, not the padded active figure, because the balloonReserve + earlyoom + cgroup handle spikes and the minAvailableMB floor is the real backstop. This is a THROTTLE (how fast we approach the floor), not a safety limit. (Earlier 600 was a cgroup-peak-incl-cache artifact; 400 over-padded.)
_notes.balloonReserveMB: Headroom for runaway growth of ALREADY-ADMITTED agents — including their CHILD toolchains (gradle/JVM daemons on candela days), which the claude-proc accounting cannot see. Cut 8->4G on 2026-07-01 morning; RESTORED to 8G the same day after the 16:06 systemd-oomd kill: fleets admitted under the 4G reserve grew ~10GB of build-tool memory and oomd killed the shared Ghostty scope at 70% mem+swap. Admission math is spawn-time-only; this reserve is what absorbs post-admission growth. Loosen only inside a launch-dreamteam.sh MemoryMax scope.
_notes.scopeToDreamteam: false = GLOBAL safety net on every agent spawn (recommended — 06-30 spanned multiple sessions). true = only acts when a team marker is active (state/active).

_notes.enforce: true = reuse-gate BLOCKS a fresh spawn when an idle teammate can take the task (reuse via SendMessage = zero new RAM + warm context). Override per-spawn with 'FRESH-SPAWN: <reason>' in the prompt. false = disable the gate entirely.

dashboard._notes: Local mission-control dashboard service (issue #11). scripts/dashboard-server.py serves templates/dashboard.html + /api/data (dashboard-data.sh --json --all-teams, 5s cache) + /api/version. host defaults to 127.0.0.1 (localhost only, safe); set "0.0.0.0" to expose on the LAN (homelab norm — opt-in). Manage via scripts/dashboard-ctl.sh {install|start|stop|status|logs} — a systemctl --user unit (systemd/dreamteam-dashboard.service, MemoryMax 256M). Readers default to 8383/127.0.0.1 if this section is absent, per the file's baked-defaults idiom; env DREAMTEAM_DASHBOARD_PORT/HOST override at runtime.

spawn._notes: spawn-standards.sh (PreToolUse Agent|Task, first in chain) blocks teammate spawns that violate the skill's conventions: names must be <dreamname>-<role> from the dream roster, and typed personas (luna/morpheus/lucid/nebula/oracle + the hypnos/nyx manager roles) must spawn with subagent_type dreamteam:<name>. Escape per-spawn: STANDARDS-EXEMPT: <reason> in the prompt. Added 2026-07-01 after coordinators kept drifting from the naming/type conventions; hypnos/nyx added to the roster + typed list 2026-07-09 (manager-roles R1) so a typeless hypnos-agent-manager can no longer slip the gate persona-less.

managers._notes: Per-team manager roles (Hypnos + Nyx) — spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-manager-roles-design.md §4. minTeamSize = the planned working-agent count at or above which the startup sequence spawns the managers FIRST (before the working wave); below it, Sandman wears both hats (current behavior). Hypnos (agent/comms manager) spawns at >= minTeamSize; Nyx (resource/memory manager) is gated SEPARATELY on scale/memory-pressure per the spec, not on this worker count alone. Managers are typed teammates (subagent_type dreamteam:hypnos|nyx — spawn-standards.sh enforces the type so the persona system prompt loads), never forks, and count against the memory budget like any agent (a 3-worker team's true footprint is 5 agents, +~600 MB at the default perAgentMB). Readers default to minTeamSize 3 if this section is absent, per the file's baked-defaults idiom.

worktree._notes: worktree-guard.sh (PreToolUse Edit|Write in TEAMMATE sessions) blocks writes outside an agent's assigned worktree (its team-config cwd) when that cwd is under .claude/worktrees/. Shared-checkout spawns (cwd not a worktree) are unaffected. Escape: orchestrator sets enforce=false, or the agent escalates via SendMessage. Added 2026-07-01 — converts the skill's #1 failure mode (2 collision incidents) from prompt discipline to harness law.

scope._notes: Caps for BOTH containment paths: launch-dreamteam.sh (whole-session scope) and scope-attach.sh (autoAttach=true: every spawn attaches THIS PROJECT'S live agent procs into dreamteam-<project>.scope via AttachProcessesToUnit — per-project since #19, so scope==project for fleet attribution and one project's runaway can't throttle another's fleet; before that, one shared dreamteam-agents.scope held everyone, added after the 2026-07-01 16:06 oomd kill). Name precedence: DREAMTEAM_SCOPE_NAME env > scope.name (add here to pin) > dreamteam-<repo basename, sanitized>. Caps apply PER SCOPE — N projects can nominally reserve N*MemoryHigh; the host RED-tier floor and systemd-oomd remain the global guards. MemoryHigh = throttle; MemoryMax = hard kill inside the agents' cgroup (orchestrators stay outside and survive); MemorySwapMax bounds the team's swap. Size to leave the GUI/host a few GB.

_notes.enabled: The OPTIONAL local-model (ollama) lane — issue #16. DEFAULT false = the whole lane is a clean no-op and NOTHING in the default path touches ollama. scripts/local-model.sh reads this ==false-safe: only a literal `true` arms it (absent/null/false all stay off), sidestepping the jq `// true` trap that once made speech.enabled un-disableable. This is NOT a third agent-brain tier — JP's 2026-07-01 ruling stands (agent reasoning = Fable 5 → latest Opus; no sonnet/haiku/local). The lane is ONLY for work that doesn't need frontier reasoning: mechanical bulk, cron summaries (morning-briefing/self-audit), embeddings, and pre-filter triage. Anything it generates that lands in a repo goes through the oracle (Fable/Opus) before commit. Env DREAMTEAM_LOCAL_ENABLED overrides per-invocation.
_notes.model: Default generation model. qwen2.5:14b-instruct-q4_K_M (~9 GB, fits the 11 GiB 2080 Ti) is on-disk here and issue-endorsed. The lane NEVER auto-pulls — a missing model just fails the call (exit 3 → caller falls back to cloud). For a dedicated coder model, `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b` and repoint this. Env DREAMTEAM_LOCAL_MODEL / --model override.
_notes.embedModel: Embeddings model for the --embed path (palace/dreamteam search). nomic-embed-text:v1.5 (768-dim) is on-disk. Env DREAMTEAM_LOCAL_EMBED_MODEL override.
_notes.host: ollama HTTP API base URL. Env DREAMTEAM_LOCAL_HOST override.
_notes.timeoutSec: Per-request curl cap in seconds (a cold model load can take tens of seconds on the first call). Env DREAMTEAM_LOCAL_TIMEOUT override.
_notes.reserveMB: MiB of RAM the admission math holds back for the resident ollama model WHEN the lane is armed (enabled=true) — issue #37. mem-gate.sh, mem-budget.sh, and dashboard-data.sh all subtract this from available RAM before dividing by perAgentMB, exactly as balloonReserveMB reserves for post-admission growth. It's a FORWARD-LOOKING reserve: the model load is latent/bursty (free's `available` only reflects it once resident, and after keep_alive expiry it unloads), so we reserve whether or not it's currently loaded. Default 9000 = worst case, a ~9 GB model FULLY CPU-resident (matches the largest on-disk model). On this GPU box the weights live in VRAM (not system RAM), so the true RAM cost is far lower (~1-3 GB) — lower this to reclaim agent headroom if the model reliably stays GPU-resident. Zero effect while enabled=false (the default). Keep in sync across the three readers (test-roster.sh defaults-agreement guard enforces this).
_notes.memoryAccounting: RESOLVED in #37 via reserveMB above (was the #16-bullet-3 deferral). The chosen lever is a config reserve subtracted from the admission budget when armed — NOT attaching the ollama server to the dreamteam scope: ollama is a shared SYSTEM daemon (own systemd unit), so pulling it into dreamteam-<project>.scope would (a) make a scope OOM-kill take ollama down with the team, and (b) not change the free-based admission math anyway. The reserve throttles spawns to leave RAM for the model; the scope + earlyoom remain the containment backstops.

speech._notes: Voice attention seam (scripts/speak.sh, issue #9) + OFFLINE FALLBACK (issue #17). engine = primary TTS engine (default azure); fallback = ordered engines tried, in order, ONLY when the one before exits non-zero — e.g. set ["piper"] to keep the house audible when the cloud is down or credential-less. Default [] = single-engine azure = byte-for-byte the pre-#17 behavior (zero change when Azure is healthy). speak.sh sets SPEECH_ENGINE=<engine> per attempt and the engine's voice env (azure→AZURE_SPEECH_VOICE, piper→PIPER_VOICE); speech-to-cli's local-TTS support must honor SPEECH_ENGINE and exit non-zero on synth failure for the hop to fire (missing creds already exits 1; the cloud-unreachable path must too — see that repo's issue). voices.<alias>.<engine> keeps ONE identity across engines: the davis/sandman alias is Davis on Azure and Davis-adjacent (ryan) on piper; override here. timeoutSec caps each engine's synth+playback in seconds (default 180; was a fixed 10s that truncated long utterances). enabled=false mutes all voice (default on). ttsPath overrides the tts.py location (default ~/Projects/speech-to-cli/tts.py). STT (faster-whisper) reuses the same SPEECH_ENGINE seam when voice-reply lands — out of scope for #17.
